title: Arrays order element-wise with a NULL element lowest, in `<` and in sorts
verdict: `list_null_order`: NULL element smallest, `[1, NULL] < [1, 2]` true; ascending sorts NULL list first
description: Arrays compare element by element, a shorter prefix first; a NULL element is smaller than any value and equal to another NULL. So `array(1, NULL) < array(1, 2)` is true (never NULL), `array(NULL) < array(0)` true, and `array(1, NULL) = array(1, NULL)` true. Ascending sorts put a NULL array first, then `[]`, `[NULL]`, `[1]`, `[1, NULL]`, `[1, 2]`; `min` and `max` of arrays follow the same order.
Inside an array, `sort_array` puts NULLs first ascending and last descending; `array_sort` puts them last.
reference: `list_null_order`: NULL where a NULL element decides `<`, and `GREATEST` in `ORDER BY` (#207). Spark orders the NULL element lowest in both, so a writer refuses or rewrites list comparisons where an element may be NULL.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `array(1, 2, NULL, 4, 5) = array(1, 2, NULL, 4, 5)` is true (the row is kept)

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
